messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx/error rate detected for /v1/generate (inference-us-west-2 pool). 5m error rate 18% (baseline ~0.2%). Alert id: 1768502468. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/infer/d/alerts/1768502468
emma_dev: seeing it on dashboards — spike started ~2026-02-14T12:13Z. Tail latencies also up. Looks like many requests hitting model-runner and getting 5xx/segfaults.
sanjay_oncall: I'm taking pager. paging @dmitri_eng @kevin_sre. starting triage now.
dmitri_eng: pulling logs from newest runner nodes. prelim: repeated segfaults from model_runner + intermittent GPU OOMs on node infer-usw2-12. grabbing stack traces.
dmitri_eng: logs snippet: ```[2026-02-14T12:13:05Z] model_runner.cpp:457] segfault (SIGSEGV) at 0x0
[2026-02-14T12:13:05Z] runtime: GPU 3 OOM during forward pass (alloc 1.2GB), triggering abort
#0 0x7f9d1a2a libattention.so +0x12a4
#1 0x7f9d2b3c model_runner +0x3b2
#2 0x55f0c4a executor +0x1f4
```
kevin_sre: seeing node eviction loops and kernel crashes. marking infer-usw2-12 out of rotation now: `infractl node drain infer-usw2-12`
kevin_sre: also increasing node-level logging and enabling cgroup memory limits to avoid cascade.
opslead: recommend immediate traffic shift to fallback lower-memory model variant and temporary scale-up. propose: `redwood route update --route /v1/generate --model rwd-llama-mini-1.0 --rollout 100% --reason \"mitigation: kernel OOM\"`
sanjay_oncall: applying route change and scaling permissive capacity. will keep 1:1 oncall until stable.
caroline_support: customer-impact: Support ticket surge — AcmeCorp, Healthly, Chatly reporting 500s. AcmeCorp hitting SLA window (5m error >5%). Notifying AMs and drafting customer message.
dmitri_eng: quick root-cause hypothesis: recent quant-kernel merge (2026-02-13) underreports GPU memory usage when KV cache grows -> late OOMs and corrupted state leading to segfaults. reproduced locally with kv-heavy prompt.
dmitri_eng: repro logs: ```repro-run --model rwd-llama-quant --prompt large-prefix
[RUN] KV cache growth to 5.6GB (reported 3.2GB) -> cudaMalloc failed -> segfault at memcpy
```
kevin_sre: starting canary rollback of quant-kernel on a single canary cluster. If green, we'll rollback globally. also kicking autoscaler to add capacity: `autoscaler set --pool inference-usw2 --min 12 --max 80`
emma_dev: traffic shifted to fallback model. errors down to ~1.5% over last 3m. latencies back near baseline. monitoring closely. :thumbsup:
sanjay_oncall: good. maintain watch for 30m. postmortem owner: dmitri_eng. Hotfix plan: rollback quant-kernel + patch memory accounting + add kv-cache upper-bound circuit-breaker.
opslead: action items logged: 1) complete rollback and verify 30m 2) push memory-accounting fix + unit tests 3) add canary gating that monitors GPU mem headroom + KV growth 4) add routing circuit-breaker to failover to low-mem variants earlier 5) update runbook with this scenario. I'll create tasks in tracker and link here.
caroline_support: customer comms pushed to AcmeCorp + Healthly; waiting response from Chatly. will post status update to status.redwood.com once we confirm full recovery.
dmitri_eng: canary rollback succeeded, no segfaults on canary for 20m. preparing global rollback now (staggered). starting patch branch for quant-kernel fix; will schedule hotpatch deploy after rollback stabilizes.
kevin_sre: global rollback in progress (staggered by AZ). continuing to drain any nodes showing repeat evictions.
incident-bot: Severity downgraded to P2 — mitigation active, monitoring. 5xx rate trending to baseline.
emma_dev: confirmed: 5xx < 0.5% across the pool, tail latency normalized. closing live-mitigation cycle.
sanjay_oncall: leaving notes for handoff: monitor for 2h, if any reoccurrence escalate to oncall #2. Postmortem and timeline assigned to dmitri_eng, support comms to caroline_support.
opslead: thanks all — nice fast coordination. will follow up with an RCA with timeline and CL/patch link.
incident-bot: Incident recorded: 1768502468. Closing thread to active triage; incident page will include timeline + logs + remediation steps.
